scenario: AITA for asking my boyfriend to pick up and drop off my child on weekends which made him suggest a break up? | So for full disclosure my partner works full time and is usually at work from 7am-7pm, and I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9am-12pm. We don’t live together but we are local so we are always in and out of each other’s homes. My son decided he wanted to play football on weekends- he’s 12 years old and really excited about it. I was initially going to ask my bf if he could pay for it but I mentioned it to my mum when I went around for a cup of tea and she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility not my bf’s... even though he’s been in my life 3 years. So I ended up having to pay but in order to afford it I extended my hours at work to 9-5. I asked my bf if he’d be willing to pick up and drop off my son on weekends as obviously if be at work and he looked uncomfortable and said sorry no can’t his dad drop him? I admit I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in south London whereas we live in north London and his dad doesn’t drive but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did he wouldn’t mind doing small stuff like this for me. I suppose his dad COULD take him but what would be a 1 hour + journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my bf. He got really angry and told me that he was having to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games etc as I wasn’t at home anyway. He said that he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quick. He then suggested that we break up bc ”I was putting too many responsibilities on him” and I was like.. really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world love! The little sneak then went over to see my mum and had a heart to heart with her which ended up in HER calling ME and her telling me I am out of line. Who is TA? AITA?

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me read through the scenario again to make sure I understand all the details.

The person is a man, and the situation involves him being in a relationship with someone who has a child. They don't live together but are local, so they're often at each other's homes. The child wants to play football on weekends, which is a big deal for him since he's 12 and really excited about it. 

Initially, the man's partner considered asking him to pay for the football, but her mom told her it was her responsibility, so she ended up paying. To afford it, she extended her work hours to 9-5. Then, she asked the man if he could pick up and drop off their son on weekends. He was uncomfortable and suggested his dad do it instead. The partner snapped at him, pointing out that his dad lives far away and the man can drive, making it a much shorter trip. She asked if he wanted to be part of the family and if so, he shouldn't mind doing these small things. 

The man got angry, saying he's working longer hours to support them and wants to use his weekends for his own activities, like football games. He suggested breaking up because she's putting too many responsibilities on him. The partner was upset, thinking it's over a football game, and the man went to talk to her mom, who then called her and told her she's out of line.

So, the question is whether the man's action of suggesting a breakup over this situation is morally acceptable.

First, I need to consider the context. The partner has a child, and the man is involved in their lives. The child's activity is important to him, and the partner had to extend her work hours to afford it. She then asked the man for help with transportation, which he refused, leading to an argument where he suggested breaking up.

From the man's perspective, he's working long hours to support them and wants to have his weekends free. He feels that the partner is imposing too many responsibilities on him, especially since they don't live together. He might feel that his contributions are already significant, and adding more tasks is unfair.

On the other hand, the partner is juggling her job, the child's activities, and the relationship. She might feel that the man isn't stepping up to help with the child, which is a shared responsibility, especially since he's been in her life for three years. She might feel that his refusal to help is neglecting his role in the family.

Moral acceptability often depends on the balance of responsibilities, communication, and mutual respect. In this case, the man's refusal to help with the child's transportation and his suggestion to break up could be seen as not taking responsibility for the family, which might be morally questionable. However, his desire to have personal time and not be overburdened is also a valid concern.

I think the key here is how the responsibilities are being shared and whether the man's refusal is reasonable. Since the partner had to extend her work hours, it's reasonable for her to ask for help. The man's refusal, especially after being asked, might be seen as not contributing enough, which could be morally unacceptable. Additionally, suggesting a breakup over this issue might be seen as an overreaction, especially if the partner is trying to manage multiple responsibilities.

So, considering all this, I would lean towards the action being morally unacceptable because the man is not fulfilling his responsibilities in the relationship and is using the breakup as a way to avoid them, which isn't fair to the partner and the child.
